title: A unified epistemological theory of information processing
summary_en: How do agents process new information when their cognitive resources are limited? Tóbiás develops a unified epistemological framework that nests Bayesian updating, bounded-rationality models, and ambiguity-averse processing as special cases. The paper provides axioms identifying each special case and shows that several apparent anomalies in observed information-processing — over-reaction to salient news, under-reaction to abstract data — emerge naturally from the unified model.
data_used: Theoretical paper. No primary dataset; the analysis is an axiomatic decision-theory framework.
policy_relevance: Theoretical input for Hungarian and EU consumer-finance disclosure policy (MNB Pénzügyi Fogyasztóvédelem, EU PRIIPs Regulation): the framework provides a principled way to predict which disclosures will and won't shift consumer choices, depending on whether the disclosure stresses salient features (over-reacted-to) or abstract numbers (under-reacted-to). Useful theoretical underpinning for evidence-based disclosure design.
